claimBoundary: This glossary records only bounded terminology and source-attributed statements from the reviewed MAPO interview. It is not page-stable book evidence, a complete Symbolic Algorithm specification, or runtime attribution.

entries.sourceLocation: MAPO interview Q&A after the interview heading
entries.boundedDefinition: The interview presents Algoritmi Simbolik as the mathematics or inner mathematics of the symbol and connects it with universal symbolic structures.
entries.englishExplanation: This is a source-attributed description of the term, not a reconstruction of a complete algorithm.

claimBoundary.fact: The MAPO interview attributes this description to Petro Zheji.
claimBoundary.inference: The statement points to a symbolic-mathematical account of symbols.
unknown: Whether his published books define the term identically.
Whether the interview provides a complete formal algorithm specification.
Whether the complete method has additional steps, operands, or constraints.
Whether any current Open Instrument runtime implements it faithfully.

notes: No pseudo-code, formal grammar, or complete algorithm is stored.

entries.sourceLocation: MAPO answer explaining the included third
entries.boundedDefinition: The interview identifies Kodi E with the included third and associates it with a supreme or mystical centre.
entries.englishExplanation: The interview relates Code E to an included-third concept without defining a complete formal operator.

claimBoundary.fact: The MAPO interview attributes this relationship between Kodi E and the included third to Petro Zheji.
claimBoundary.inference: Code E is presented as part of the interview's included-third explanation.
unknown: Whether the published books give a fuller or different definition.
What formal inputs, outputs, or transitions the code has.
Whether current Open Instrument Code E fields are equivalent to the interview concept.

notes: No algebraic identity or runtime mapping is asserted.

entries.sourceLocation: MAPO answer contrasting Codes E and F
entries.boundedDefinition: The interview records an included-third side of the contrast and relates it to Kodi E.

claimBoundary.fact: The interview contrasts an included third with an excluded third and relates the included side to Kodi E.
claimBoundary.inference: The included-third label provides a compact description of one side of the interview's Code E/Code F relationship.
unknown: Whether the included/excluded relationship has a formal logical equivalence.
Whether the Latin label appears in the published books with the same meaning.
Whether current runtime logic implements this relationship.

entries.sourceLocation: MAPO question asking whether the algorithm can exist in other languages
entries.boundedDefinition: The interview records an answer that the Symbolic Algorithm can be found in other languages and that sciences can be turned to the Symbolic Algorithm.
entries.englishExplanation: This records a source statement about intended applicability, not empirical validation across languages or sciences.

claimBoundary.fact: The interview attributes a claim of applicability beyond Albanian to Petro Zheji.
claimBoundary.inference: The statement presents the method as not limited to one language or domain.
unknown: Whether empirical validation exists across languages or sciences.
The operational criteria for applying the method outside Albanian.
Whether Open Instrument should implement or test this claim.

notes: Applicability is recorded as a source statement only; no scientific validation is implied.
